requirement: bml-inference-pipeline 8.6 (external-weight projection prerequisite; full integration remains open)

implementation.runtime: Explicit external-constant mode requires an empty stored pool, validates references against a declared count, counts borrowed values in GraphLimits, and requires the same count at execution. Owned and external execution APIs do not silently substitute for each other.
implementation.compiler: compile_row measures the deterministic BMLTransformer expansion size with a fixed-size probe, rejects node-budget/size overflow before building the row, and emits Var input references and Const external weight references with no owned values.
implementation.execution: A serialized BML-only row template is loaded and executed with decoded rows from the mapped F32 causal fixture. Different inputs and different rows produce the independent coordinate-selection oracle.
implementation.store_documentation: RpnOp::StoreResult documentation now matches the unchanged runtime: pop offset, pop value, consume both. Tests duplicate the retained result explicitly.

verification.contexts: Wrong constant counts, inputs and buffer shapes fail before writes; owned-pool mixing and implicit execution modes fail; zero external constants remain an explicit mode.
verification.bounds: Inclusive external constant references, zero-iteration loop references, value/stack budgets and overflow; inclusive exact row node budgets.
verification.arithmetic: No FAdd, FMul or opaque operators; One, Var, Const, Bml and stack operations only.

limitations: No weights are serialized in the row program; decoding a mapped row and converting F32 to F64 still allocates caller-owned scratch storage.
The integration fixture is F32, not a new quantized-model correctness claim.
Signed BML numerical range and rounding differ from native IEEE arithmetic.
Row templates are unrolled and have linear bytecode storage, unlike the native loop profile.
This does not replace the full GGUF transformer DAG or the existing causal artifact execution profile.
